natural_body: SMB 40% discounts lifted acquisition and near-term revenue but cut retention 12%.

first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and we have strong prior evidence that shorter onboarding and reduced signup friction both drove durable adoption gains (memory_86, memory_31). Activation messaging also showed promise (memory_91). Rather than chase promotional pricing—which memory_73 shows risks retention severely—we should double down on the mechanic that builds sustainable engagement: removing friction from entry and early experience. This addresses both the completion decline and activation decline through a proven lever, avoids the retention damage of discounting, and positions us defensively against price-focused competitor pressure by competing on ease and speed-to-value instead. Verifying memory_86 and memory_31 will confirm the magnitude and durability of onboarding improvements before we commit. Enterprise_sales_assist is lower priority given the SMB-heavy nature of the current competitive threat.
